findings.evidence: 1.29 PFLOP / ~1.08 s ≈ 1.19 PFLOPS demand > 0.989 PFLOPS H100 peak; with the attention term included (~1.51 PFLOP) the demand is ~1.40 PFLOPS
findings.issue: Units inconsistency inside one table cell. The first sentence uses the noun 'PFLOP' for the work quantity (1.29 PFLOP) and 'PFLOPS' for the rate (1.19 PFLOPS) — correct — but the phrase '~1.51 PFLOP' is then described as the attention-included 'demand', and the next clause converts it to '1.40 PFLOPS'. The same numeric quantity is written with two different unit suffixes (PFLOP vs PFLOPS) in one sentence, and the second value (1.40) is a rate, not a work quantity, which is easy to misread as a second work figure.
findings.fix_instruction: Split the cell into two clauses with explicit unit labels: '1.29 PFLOP (work) / ~1.08 s ≈ 1.19 PFLOPS (rate) > 0.989 PFLOPS H100 peak. Adding the attention term gives ~1.51 PFLOP of work, i.e. ~1.40 PFLOPS of required rate.' Never write 'the demand is ~1.51 PFLOP' — a demand is a rate, so it should always be PFLOPS.

findings.evidence: Ch. 2 §2.3, "Scope of the single-host premise": "the capacity question — how many such hosts to absorb λ = 40 rps, where in-flight concurrency λ·W ≈ 344 at the ~8.6 s service time — is answered later (Ch 16–17)"
findings.issue: Cross-reference defect: the occupancy arithmetic (λ·W at the canonical W) is derived in Ch. 4 §4.3 and Table 4-2 (pp. 66, 76), not only in Ch. 16–17. Ch. 2 forward-references the answer while the derivation sits earlier; the same page also states '1 host with 8×H100 GPUs' as a premise, which is a canonical-scenario assumption introduced in Ch. 4 — a circular cross-reference to a scenario defined later.
findings.fix_instruction: Cite Ch. 4 §4.3 (Table 4-2) as the source of the ~344 occupancy and the canonical host definition, in addition to Ch. 16–17 for the sizing consequence.

findings.evidence: Ch. 2 §2.1: "The full prefill also has a substantial linear-in-L component — the weight-matmul FLOPs, 2NL (where N = model parameters and L = tokens processed) — which does not grow quadratically; the quadratic term is the dense-attention pairwise component, developed in Ch 8 and Ch 22."
findings.issue: Cross-reference defect: 'Ch 8 and Ch 22' omit the period used elsewhere ('Ch. 8', 'Ch. 22'), and more substantively the quadratic-attention term's derivation is stated in the book's own prefill-FLOP convention at Ch. 2 Table 2-2's scope note (p. 27: 'case (ii) 2NL plus the full-square attention term 4 · nlayers · L2 · d; case (iii) ... defined in full at Ch 8 §3.3'). The convention note itself uses the same 'Ch 8' form without a period, so the inconsistency is book-wide and must be fixed at the root, not per instance.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalize all chapter references to 'Ch. N' (with period) throughout, including Table 2-2's scope note and the Preface; run a global find/replace for 'Ch N' patterns lacking the period.

findings.evidence: Ch. 2 §2.7: "Effect of quantization on decode bandwidth vs prefill FLOPs. Int4 or FP8 quantization reduces the weight bytes (e.g., 70B at FP8 = 70 GB instead of 140 GB), which directly lowers the HBM read demand in decode; it does not reduce the algorithmic operation count of the matmuls (the 2 × params × tokens FLOPs are approximately unchanged), though lower precision can raise the effective throughput of the tensor cores at which those ops run."
findings.issue: Arithmetic/labelling omission: the '70B at FP8 = 70 GB' figure is stated inline without an evidence tag, in a chapter whose other hardware and scenario constants are tagged, and it is load-bearing (it is the basis of the decode-bandwidth improvement claim and appears again in Ch. 7's Table 7-2 and §7.6). Under the Preface's rule it should be [canonical scenario][DERIVED] (70B × 1 byte) or [1P][DERIVED] depending on whether the 70B is the canonical teaching geometry — and here the 70B is the canonical scenario's model, so the provenance must be [canonical scenario].
findings.fix_instruction: Tag the figure inline as [canonical scenario][DERIVED] (70B × 1 B/param) and make sure the same 70 GB figure carries the same tag in Ch. 7 §7.6 and Table 7-2.

findings.evidence: "~0.47 s at 35% MFU" (PDF 54, untagged); likewise "one H100 sustains ~2,472 tok/s at 35% MFU" (PDF 104), "8 × 0.989 PFLOPS × 0.35 ÷ 140 GFLOP/token = 19,780 tok/s per host" (PDF 116), "~2.77 PFLOP/s (35% MFU, Ch 8 §3)" (PDF 146).
findings.issue: 35% MFU is a load-bearing planning constant — it derives ~2,472 tok/s per GPU, ~19,800 tok/s per host, ~2.77 PFLOP/s sustained prefill and every host screen built on them — yet carries no provenance/epistemic tag at any inline occurrence in the excerpt, contrary to the book's rule that 'a number that any downstream figure depends on is labeled'.
findings.fix_instruction: Tag the constant once at first use (e.g. [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] or [2°][FACT] with a named source) and have later occurrences defer to that anchor.

findings.evidence: Text: 'TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill. The canonical 1.2 s budget covers only the two dominant modeled terms...'.
findings.issue: Cross-chapter Consistency: Preface (Pg 34) defines TTFT with 4 terms, then budgets 1.2s with 2 terms. Ch 2 (Pg 199) repeats the 4-term formula but budgets 1.2s. This implies 'admission' and 'tokenization' take 0s in this model.
findings.fix_instruction: Explicitly state 'assuming negligible admission/tokenization' to avoid confusion with real-world non-zero latency.

PDF p. 28: "weight-only arithmetic intensity ≈ 9,200 FLOP/byte — an upper bound that omits the ~24 GB KV write; adding that write to the denominator lowers the intensity to ≈ 7,850 FLOP/byte (Ch 8)". PDF p. 145: "adding the quadratic attention term raises it to ~10.8K, activation traffic lowers it — either way ≫ 295".
findings.issue: The same prefill arithmetic-intensity quantity is stated on inconsistent bases. Chapter 2 says the KV write must be added to the denominator, giving ≈7,850 FLOP/byte, while Table 6-1’s footnote gives ≈10.8K after adding attention FLOPs and mentions only activation traffic as a lowering term. The regime conclusion is unaffected, but the numerical accounting convention is not consistent across chapters.
findings.fix_instruction: State one denominator rule in both places. Either present ~10.8K explicitly as a numerator-only intermediate and then reconcile it to ~7,850 FLOP/byte once the ~24 GB KV write is included, or replace the Table 6-1 footnote value with the book’s canonical full-traffic intensity.
